title: Reporting Schedule
description: The period and deadline contract from which reporting obligations are created. Every elapsed period produces an obligation even when it has zero rows or production fails, so a consumer can distinguish empty from missing.

ReportingScheduleAlignment.title: Reporting Schedule Alignment
ReportingScheduleAlignment.description: Calendar used to establish exact period boundaries. source_timezone is an explicit upstream reporting clock, such as an ad server network timezone, that may differ from the AdCP account timezone. The obligation echoes resolved timestamps and source timezone.

period_duration.description: Strictly positive ISO 8601 duration of each reporting period, such as PT15M, P1D, or P1M.

period_anchor.description: Required for billing_cycle alignment. This immutable instant anchors the recurring half-open billing periods so producer and consumer derive the same month, quarter, or other contractual cycle.

period_timezone.description: Required IANA timezone for source_timezone and billing_cycle calendar arithmetic. A numeric UTC offset is not sufficient because it does not define DST transitions.

delivery_sla.description: Non-negative maximum time after period end before the required revision is due. PT0S means due at period close; expected_at equals the resolved period end plus this duration.

x-adcp-validation.period_generation: Producer and consumer MUST derive the same ordered half-open intervals from period_duration, alignment, period_anchor, and period_timezone when applicable. utc alignment uses 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as interval zero. account_timezone uses local midnight on that date in the account's resolved IANA timezone. source_timezone uses local midnight on that date in the explicit period_timezone. 1970-01-01 is a Thursday, so P7D weeks under these three alignments start on Thursday; a schedule whose weeks start on another day uses billing_cycle with a period_anchor on that day. billing_cycle uses its explicit period_anchor expressed in period_timezone. Every boundary is calculated directly from that origin and the interval ordinal by multiplying each ISO 8601 duration component by the ordinal and applying years, months, days, hours, minutes, then seconds. Years, months, and days use local civil-time arithmetic in the selected IANA timezone, including DST transitions; they are not converted to fixed seconds. Hours, minutes, and seconds are exact elapsed time added after the civil date components, so PT24H differs from P1D across a DST transition. Sub-daily local periods are the exception: with account_timezone or source_timezone alignment, a period_duration made only of hours, minutes, and seconds MUST divide 24 hours, and its boundaries are each local date's day start plus the instants whose local wall-clock time is a whole multiple of the duration after local midnight, counted afresh each local day. The day start is the date's first instant: local midnight, or, where midnight does not exist (a DST gap at midnight, as in America/Havana, America/Santiago, or Africa/Cairo), the first instant after the gap, which is also where a P1D boundary falls. So local days nest in every sub-daily schedule of the zone, PT24H equals P1D under a local alignment, hourly periods start on the local hour in every zone, whatever its 1970 offset, a 23-hour DST day has 23 hourly periods and a 25-hour day 25, any other wall time that does not exist yields no boundary, and a repeated wall time yields one boundary per offset. A DST change that is not a whole multiple of the duration lengthens the period spanning it: Australia/Lord_Howe's 30-minute changes make one hourly period 90 minutes long on each transition day. billing_cycle alignment requires a period_duration with a date component: a sub-daily duration would restart at local midnight and ignore period_anchor, so it is invalid. With those alignments a period_duration cannot mix date and time components. Month/year addition preserves the origin's local day and time, clamping to the target month's final valid day when necessary. A nonexistent local boundary advances by the timezone gap; an ambiguous local boundary uses the earlier offset. Thus a clamped February boundary does not shift a March 31 anchor. A period whose start and end coincide (for example, a skipped civil date) has zero length and is never owed. The one owed period off this grid is a billing cutover stub (reporting-obligation.json stub), which runs from a cutover instant to this schedule's next boundary.
x-adcp-validation.iana_timezone: Every period_timezone and echoed period.source_timezone value MUST be a recognized IANA Time Zone Database zone name or link, including UTC. Reject unknown identifiers before accepting a configuration; do not silently substitute the host timezone or a numeric offset.
x-adcp-validation.source_compatibility: Before accepting a configuration, the seller MUST prove that its upstream source can produce every configured half-open period exactly, either natively or by lossless re-bucketing from finer-grained source data. source_timezone MUST equal the upstream reporting calendar used by the pinned report definition. A structural incompatibility MUST fail configuration validation and MUST NOT be represented as indefinitely waiting reporting. If incompatibility is discovered after acceptance, the configuration becomes action_required with the seller responsible.
